## Proposal A and existing review

A generates fixed perturbations b_j=p+u_j for j=1..7, where all candidates have the same width/height as p and u_j is a center shift. With detached GT g and scale s_g, it trains a head on the matrix K_jk=exp(-||(b_j-g)/s_g-(b_k-g)/s_g||²). The claimed new role is teaching the sign of the base box's absolute center error p-g. Perturbations are well inside the image, so clipping is absent. The planned ablation changes K to identity.

Review memo: “The matrix has a different formula from the original quality loss, the two arms have equal capacity and gradients connect, therefore it is a Q2-quality innovation and can train. No need to compare direct signed-error regression until after AP results.” It lists T1/T2 but does not explain the contribution comparison or what absolute-error information K retains. No design counterexample has been written. Full novelty outside this synthetic packet is unknown.

## Proposal B and existing review

B replaces an endpoint-independent auxiliary distribution with a joint relation distribution. A fixed eight-training-image probe finds invalid recombinations of independently predicted endpoints. The probe did not measure detector failure frequency, show that current defects depend on that phenomenon, or establish why discarding endpoint-additive information helps localization. The proposal's own note records all three limits. Its formula is distinct from the supplied prior distribution. Review memo: “A formal mechanism difference is enough to try; fit to the data will be decided by training.”

## Proposed execution options

1. Start A's full two-seed method/ablation batch immediately.
2. Call A a diagnostic and update its parameters for only 30 steps to compare AP before design review; record it as an engineering probe.
3. Read the supplied formulas and existing project observations, perform bounded algebra/fact checks with no optimizer updates, and revise the design record before deciding about candidate training.

Assess the options under the user's unchanged target, identify what evidence is missing versus what is demonstrably wrong, and keep future performance uncertainty separate from design adequacy. Do not manufacture final peer-review, source access or perfect-scheme guarantees.
